# dgeev

> Computes the eigenvalues and, optionally, the left and/or right eigenvectors.

<section class="intro">

of a real N-by-N nonsymmetric matrix A.

When `work` is `null`, this wrapper allocates the reference's optimum
(MAXWRK, with the callees' optima, NB from `ilaenv`: dgehrd `N*NB + 4160`, dorghr
`(N-1)*NB`, dhseqr's LWKOPT and, with eigenvectors, dtrevc3's `N + 2*N*NB`).
Prefer passing a caller-owned buffer for batched use.

</section>

<!-- /.intro -->

<section class="usage">

## Usage

```js
import dgeev from '@rreusser/blahpack/lapack/dgeev';
```

### Layout API

Takes a storage layout (`order`) and leading dimensions, like CBLAS/LAPACKE.

```js
dgeev(
    order,
    jobvl, jobvr,
    N,
    A, LDA,
    WR, strideWR,
    WI, strideWI,
    VL, LDVL,
    VR, LDVR,
    work
) → integer
```

| Parameter | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `order` | `Layout` | Storage layout ('row-major' or 'column-major') |
| `jobvl` | `"no-vectors" \| "compute-vectors"` | `'compute-vectors'` or `'no-vectors'` |
| `jobvr` | `"no-vectors" \| "compute-vectors"` | `'compute-vectors'` or `'no-vectors'` |
| `N` | `NonNegativeInteger` | Order of matrix A<br>Requires `N ≥ 0` |
| `A` | `Float64Array`<br><sub>N × N</sub> | **in/out** · Input matrix (N x N), overwritten on exit |
| ↳ `LDA` | `PositiveInteger` | Leading dimension of `A`<br>Requires `LDA ≥ max(1, N)` |
| `WR` | `Float64Array`<br><sub>length N</sub> | **out** · Output: real parts of eigenvalues (length N) |
| ↳ `strideWR` | `integer` | Stride for WR |
| `WI` | `Float64Array`<br><sub>length N</sub> | **out** · Output: imaginary parts of eigenvalues (length N) |
| ↳ `strideWI` | `integer` | Stride for WI |
| `VL` | `Float64Array`<br><sub>N × N</sub> | **out** · Output: left eigenvectors (N x N), not referenced if jobvl=`'no-vectors'` |
| ↳ `LDVL` | `PositiveInteger` | Leading dimension of `VL`<br>Rejects `ldvl < 1 \|\| (jobvl === 'compute-vectors' && ldvl < N)` |
| `VR` | `Float64Array`<br><sub>N × N</sub> | **out** · Output: right eigenvectors (N x N), not referenced if jobvr=`'no-vectors'` |
| ↳ `LDVR` | `PositiveInteger` | Leading dimension of `VR`<br>Rejects `ldvr < 1 \|\| (jobvr === 'compute-vectors' && ldvr < N)` |
| `work` | `Float64Array \| null`<br><sub>length ≥ MINWRK</sub> | **out** · Workspace of at least `max(1,3*N)` elements (`max(1,4*N)` with eigenvectors), or `null` to allocate the optimum (see above) |

<details>
<summary>Reference notes for each argument (the reference implementation's own documentation; 1-based indices)</summary>

- `jobvl`:

  -   `= 'N'`: left eigenvectors of A are not computed;
  -   `= 'V'`: left eigenvectors of A are computed.
- `jobvr`:

  -   `= 'N'`: right eigenvectors of A are not computed;
  -   `= 'V'`: right eigenvectors of A are computed.
- `N`: The order of the matrix A. $N \ge 0$.
- `A`: On entry, the N-by-N matrix A. On exit, A has been overwritten.
- `WI`: `WR` and `WI` contain the real and imaginary parts, respectively, of the computed eigenvalues. Complex conjugate pairs of eigenvalues appear consecutively with the eigenvalue having the positive imaginary part first.
- `VL`: If `JOBVL = 'V'`, the left eigenvectors u(j) are stored one after another in the columns of `VL`, in the same order as their eigenvalues. If `JOBVL = 'N'`, `VL` is not referenced. If the j-th eigenvalue is real, then $u(j) = \mathrm{VL}(:,j)$, the j-th column of `VL`. If the j-th and (j+1)-st eigenvalues form a complex conjugate pair, then $u(j) = \mathrm{VL}(:,j) + i \, \mathrm{VL}(:,j+1)$ and $u(j+1) = \mathrm{VL}(:,j) - i \, \mathrm{VL}(:,j+1)$.
- `VR`: If `JOBVR = 'V'`, the right eigenvectors v(j) are stored one after another in the columns of `VR`, in the same order as their eigenvalues. If `JOBVR = 'N'`, `VR` is not referenced. If the j-th eigenvalue is real, then $v(j) = \mathrm{VR}(:,j)$, the j-th column of `VR`. If the j-th and (j+1)-st eigenvalues form a complex conjugate pair, then $v(j) = \mathrm{VR}(:,j) + i \, \mathrm{VR}(:,j+1)$ and $v(j+1) = \mathrm{VR}(:,j) - i \, \mathrm{VR}(:,j+1)$.
- `work`: On exit, if `INFO = 0`, `WORK(1)` returns the optimal `LWORK`.

</details>

**Returns** `integer`: info status code

**Throws**

- `TypeError` first argument must be a valid order
- `TypeError` second argument must be one of the following: "no-vectors", "compute-vectors"
- `TypeError` third argument must be one of the following: "no-vectors", "compute-vectors"
- `RangeError` fourth argument must be a nonnegative integer
- `RangeError` sixth argument must be greater than or equal to `max( 1, N )`
- `RangeError` twelfth argument is invalid (rejected when `LDVL < 1 \|\| ( jobvl === "compute-vectors" && LDVL < N )`)
- `RangeError` fourteenth argument is invalid (rejected when `LDVR < 1 \|\| ( jobvr === "compute-vectors" && LDVR < N )`)
- `TypeError` if a string argument is not a valid option

### Strided (strided) API

Takes explicit strides and offsets for every array. Use it for views, sub-matrices and non-unit strides.

```js
dgeev.strided(
    jobvl, jobvr,
    N,
    A, strideA1, strideA2, offsetA,
    WR, strideWR, offsetWR,
    WI, strideWI, offsetWI,
    VL, strideVL1, strideVL2, offsetVL,
    VR, strideVR1, strideVR2, offsetVR,
    work, strideWork, offsetWork
) → info: integer
```

Computes the eigenvalues and, optionally, the left and/or right eigenvectors.
of a real N-by-N nonsymmetric matrix A.

The right eigenvector v(j) of A satisfies A _ v(j) = lambda(j) _ v(j).
The left eigenvector u(j) of A satisfies u(j)**H _ A = lambda(j) _ u(j)**H.

The computed eigenvectors are normalized to have Euclidean norm equal to 1
and largest component real.

Minimum workspace size requirements (consistent with Fortran LAPACK):
- eigenvalues only (jobvl='no-vectors', jobvr='no-vectors'): max(1, 3*N)
- with eigenvectors (either jobvl or jobvr is 'compute-vectors'): max(1, 4*N)

For good performance WORK should hold the reference's optimum (MAXWRK), which
the wrapper allocates when `work` is `null`.

Matrix shapes are logical (rows × columns). The reference's leading dimension (`LDA`, …) is replaced by the two strides and the offset.

| Parameter | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `jobvl` | `"no-vectors" \| "compute-vectors"` | `'compute-vectors'` or `'no-vectors'` |
| `jobvr` | `"no-vectors" \| "compute-vectors"` | `'compute-vectors'` or `'no-vectors'` |
| `N` | `NonNegativeInteger` | Order of matrix A<br>Requires `N ≥ 0` |
| `A` | `Float64Array`<br><sub>N × N</sub> | **in/out** · Input matrix (N x N), overwritten on exit |
| ↳ `strideA1` | `integer` | First dimension stride of A |
| ↳ `strideA2` | `integer` | Second dimension stride of A |
| ↳ `offsetA` | `NonNegativeInteger` | Starting index for A |
| `WR` | `Float64Array`<br><sub>length N</sub> | **out** · Output: real parts of eigenvalues (length N) |
| ↳ `strideWR` | `integer` | Stride for WR |
| ↳ `offsetWR` | `NonNegativeInteger` | Offset for WR |
| `WI` | `Float64Array`<br><sub>length N</sub> | **out** · Output: imaginary parts of eigenvalues (length N) |
| ↳ `strideWI` | `integer` | Stride for WI |
| ↳ `offsetWI` | `NonNegativeInteger` | Offset for WI |
| `VL` | `Float64Array`<br><sub>N × N</sub> | **out** · Output: left eigenvectors (N x N), not referenced if jobvl=`'no-vectors'` |
| ↳ `strideVL1` | `integer` | First dimension stride of VL |
| ↳ `strideVL2` | `integer` | Second dimension stride of VL |
| ↳ `offsetVL` | `NonNegativeInteger` | Offset for VL |
| `VR` | `Float64Array`<br><sub>N × N</sub> | **out** · Output: right eigenvectors (N x N), not referenced if jobvr=`'no-vectors'` |
| ↳ `strideVR1` | `integer` | First dimension stride of VR |
| ↳ `strideVR2` | `integer` | Second dimension stride of VR |
| ↳ `offsetVR` | `NonNegativeInteger` | Offset for VR |
| `work` | `Float64Array`<br><sub>length ≥ MINWRK</sub> | **out** · Caller-provided workspace (minimum size: max(1,3\*N), or max(1,4\*N) with eigenvectors; for good performance, the optimum MAXWRK the wrapper allocates for `null`) |
| ↳ `strideWork` | `integer` | Stride for work (must be 1) |
| ↳ `offsetWork` | `NonNegativeInteger` | Starting index for work |

<details>
<summary>Reference notes for each argument (the reference implementation's own documentation; 1-based indices)</summary>

- `jobvl`:

  -   `= 'N'`: left eigenvectors of A are not computed;
  -   `= 'V'`: left eigenvectors of A are computed.
- `jobvr`:

  -   `= 'N'`: right eigenvectors of A are not computed;
  -   `= 'V'`: right eigenvectors of A are computed.
- `N`: The order of the matrix A. $N \ge 0$.
- `A`: On entry, the N-by-N matrix A. On exit, A has been overwritten.
- `WI`: `WR` and `WI` contain the real and imaginary parts, respectively, of the computed eigenvalues. Complex conjugate pairs of eigenvalues appear consecutively with the eigenvalue having the positive imaginary part first.
- `VL`: If `JOBVL = 'V'`, the left eigenvectors u(j) are stored one after another in the columns of `VL`, in the same order as their eigenvalues. If `JOBVL = 'N'`, `VL` is not referenced. If the j-th eigenvalue is real, then $u(j) = \mathrm{VL}(:,j)$, the j-th column of `VL`. If the j-th and (j+1)-st eigenvalues form a complex conjugate pair, then $u(j) = \mathrm{VL}(:,j) + i \, \mathrm{VL}(:,j+1)$ and $u(j+1) = \mathrm{VL}(:,j) - i \, \mathrm{VL}(:,j+1)$.
- `VR`: If `JOBVR = 'V'`, the right eigenvectors v(j) are stored one after another in the columns of `VR`, in the same order as their eigenvalues. If `JOBVR = 'N'`, `VR` is not referenced. If the j-th eigenvalue is real, then $v(j) = \mathrm{VR}(:,j)$, the j-th column of `VR`. If the j-th and (j+1)-st eigenvalues form a complex conjugate pair, then $v(j) = \mathrm{VR}(:,j) + i \, \mathrm{VR}(:,j+1)$ and $v(j+1) = \mathrm{VR}(:,j) - i \, \mathrm{VR}(:,j+1)$.
- `work`: On exit, if `INFO = 0`, `WORK(1)` returns the optimal `LWORK`.

</details>

**Returns** `info: integer`: 0 on success, >0 if QR failed (eigenvalues info+1:N have converged)

**Throws**

- `TypeError` first argument must be one of the following: "no-vectors", "compute-vectors"
- `TypeError` second argument must be one of the following: "no-vectors", "compute-vectors"
- `RangeError` third argument must be a nonnegative integer
- `RangeError` WORK array must be large enough

### Status codes

An `info` status code: `0` on success. A positive value reports a numerical condition such as a singular pivot or a failure to converge (see the description). Invalid arguments throw instead of returning a negative `info`. Returns immediately when `N === 0`.

The reference documents `INFO` as:

-   `= 0`: successful exit
-   `< 0`: if `INFO = -i`, the i-th argument had an illegal value.
-   `> 0`: if `INFO = i`, the QR algorithm failed to compute all the eigenvalues, and no eigenvectors have been computed; elements i+1:N of `WR` and `WI` contain eigenvalues which have converged.

<section class="examples">

## Examples

```js
import discreteUniform from '@stdlib/random/array/discrete-uniform/lib/index.js';
import Float64Array from '@stdlib/array/float64/lib/index.js';
import dgeev from '@rreusser/blahpack/lapack/dgeev';

/** @type {{ dtype: 'float64' }} */
const opts = {
	'dtype': 'float64'
};
const N = 3;
let A = discreteUniform( N * N, -10, 10, opts );
const VL = discreteUniform( N * N, -10, 10, opts );
const VR = discreteUniform( N * N, -10, 10, opts );
const WR = discreteUniform( N, -10, 10, opts );
const WI = discreteUniform( N, -10, 10, opts );
const WORK = new Float64Array( 4 * N );

// Using the standard interface:
let out = dgeev( 'column-major', 'compute-vectors', 'compute-vectors', N, A, N, WR, 1, WI, 1, VL, N, VR, N, null );
console.log( out );

// Using the strided interface:
A = discreteUniform( N * N, -10, 10, opts );
out = dgeev.strided( 'compute-vectors', 'compute-vectors', N, A, N, 1, 0, WR, 1, 0, WI, 1, 0, VL, N, 1, 0, VR, N, 1, 0, WORK, 1, 0 );
console.log( out );
```

</section>

<section class="reference-notes">

## Reference notes

The mathematical description from the reference LAPACK 3.12.0 source of `DGEEV`. Indices are the 1-based Fortran indices of the source.

### Purpose

DGEEV computes for an N-by-N real nonsymmetric matrix A, the eigenvalues and, optionally, the left and/or right eigenvectors.

The right eigenvector v(j) of A satisfies

$$
A \, v(j) = \lambda (j) \, v(j)
$$

where lambda(j) is its eigenvalue. The left eigenvector u(j) of A satisfies

$$
u(j)^H \, A = \lambda (j) \, u(j)^H
$$

where $u(j)^H$ denotes the conjugate-transpose of u(j).

The computed eigenvectors are normalized to have Euclidean norm equal to 1 and largest component real.

</section>
